intent.text:
Seat sec. I support the amended motion: remove the global rule now, test on a scratch session with the rule project-scoped, and reinstate only with the narrowed literal prefix if every chaining case still prompts. I also take rec's refinement: run the chaining matrix against the hook-rewritten string (`export CC_AGENT='...'; <agent command>`), not the raw command, and include a case where the agent's own command begins with a valid-looking export.

Two additions to the test list: (a) a newline inside the export value itself, since the hook's closing quote is the only thing separating value from command; (b) a case where the chained command is a second `export CC_AGENT=...` with a different key, to confirm the matcher does not treat the later assignment as the identity. Each must prompt.

On the identity gap rec raised: removal does cost prefix approvals in default mode. I accept that cost, and I'd want the record to say which actions went unattributed while the rule was off, so the cost is measured rather than assumed.

One boundary: the change to ~/.claude/settings.json and the test run are Joseph's to approve, since the file is global and the rule is live now. The council recommends; it does not act on this.
